name: Cindershift Reversible Crowd-Runner Rig
description: A complete tactical ensemble built for disappearing into Tier 2-3 foot traffic. The centerpiece is a reversible mid-thigh jacket — one side a muted brick-burgundy with worn stress lines mimicking a delivery courier's daily rig, the other a deep slate-grey with subtle hexagonal texture that reads as generic maintenance wear at a glance. The jacket features mag-detach shoulder panels, a reinforced internal holster channel along the left ribcage, and a scanner-resistant lining woven from Nullthread-X that scatters passive RFID sweeps. Beneath it, a henley-style compression shirt in dusty teal stretches over the torso, with aug-power routing channels stitched along the left sleeve for chrome-arm compatibility — a discreet zip-port at the wrist allows external device tethering without exposing hardware. Cargo trousers in deep rust-brown feature reinforced knees, two deep thigh pockets with magnetic closures, and a hidden ankle zip-pocket sized for a folding blade or med-patch stack. Footwear is low-profile synthetic leather boots with a composite toe and soft-grip sole — scuffed deliberately at the toe cap to read as working-class wear.
functionality: Reversible jacket for rapid appearance change, scanner-resistant lining, integrated left-ribcage holster channel, aug-power routing sleeve, hidden ankle pocket, magnetic thigh-pocket closures, composite-toe boots
what_it_says: This is someone who has done this long enough to stop looking like they're doing it. The outfit reads as courier or maintenance at three meters, which is exactly the point. Veterans of the runner circuit recognize the tell-tale wrist zip-port and the deliberate scuff pattern — a calling card worn with practiced indifference.
worn_by: data couriers doubling as extraction assets
manufacturer: Splitseam Workshop — a street-label operation out of the Circuit's garment district, known for reversible and quick-change tactical builds
story_hooks: A runner flips the jacket mid-pursuit through a crowded transit hub, but a sharp-eyed Helix Corp security drone has already logged both color profiles — the reversal buys thirty seconds, not escape.

The scanner-resistant lining starts degrading after exposure to an acid-rain squall in the Gray Zone, and the runner realizes mid-job that their concealed hardware is pinging every checkpoint between them and the extraction point.
A contact recognizes the Splitseam wrist zip-port and uses it as a dead-drop authentication — something was sewn into the port housing that the runner didn't know about.

physical_description.visual_profile: A complete tactical ensemble designed for anonymous urban movement. The silhouette reads as working-class utilitarian—neither bulky nor fitted—with layered functionality that blends seamlessly into Tier 2-3 foot traffic. The reversible jacket dominates: brick-burgundy courier-worn on one side, slate-grey maintenance-tech on the other. Beneath sits a teal compression layer suggesting augmentation compatibility. The overall impression is deliberate understatement—built to be forgettable.
physical_description.fit: Athletic compression through the torso with strategic room at the hips and thighs. The jacket sits mid-thigh with tailored shoulders that allow mag-panel detachment without bunching. Trousers are straight-cut with functional ease at the knees, neither slim nor baggy. Boots are low-profile, minimizing visual height signature.
physical_description.primary_material: Jacket: ballistic-weave synthetic with Nullthread-X scanner-resistant lining. Henley: performance compression blend with conductive threading. Trousers: reinforced cotton-synthetic composite. Boots: scuffed synthetic leather with composite toe reinforcement.
physical_description.texture: Jacket exterior: matte with deliberate stress creasing and worn thread-bare patches mimicking authentic wear. Interior hexagonal texture reads flat at distance. Henley: smooth stretch with subtle ribbed power-routing channels. Trousers: canvas-like finish with reinforced knee panels showing subtle thread-wear. Boots: weathered leather with dull composite toe capping.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: brick-burgundy and deep slate-grey (reversible). Secondary: dusty teal compression layer. Tertiary: rust-brown trousers. Accent: aged grey synthetic leather boots. Palette reads as low-visibility urban neutral.
physical_description.closures: Jacket: magnetic snap shoulder panels (quick-detach). Henley: discrete friction-fit aug-power zip at wrist. Trousers: traditional button fly with magnetic thigh-pocket closures and hidden ankle zip-pocket. Boots: standard lace with friction-grip sole.
distinctive_features: Reversible jacket with two distinct social-read profiles
Mag-detach shoulder panels for modular reconfiguration
Reinforced left-ribcage holster channel (integrated, invisible externally)
Aug-power routing channels stitched along compression shirt left sleeve
Wrist zip-port for device tethering without hardware exposure
Hidden ankle zip-pocket for blade/med-patch storage
Deliberately scuffed boots to signal authentic working-class wear
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 functional—expensive enough to be durable, anonymous enough to avoid attention. Price point suggests streetside custom work, not corpo manufacturing.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street operator, courier, maintenance-tier augmented personnel, or low-profile corpo asset. Wearing this signals either genuine working-class status or calculated infiltration. The reversibility suggests someone who needs to shift identities in real-time—whether for survival, employment, or evasion.
physical_description.condition_typical: Deliberately broken-in, with authentic stress wear and intentional scuffing. Never pristine; always reads as already-in-use, which is the entire design philosophy.
